title: Evaluation & Quality Gating: Optimize prompt sets, regression thresholds, A/B criteria, rollback triggers
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define product-level evaluation and quality gating requirements for Redwood Optimize. This ticket captures the canonical prompt sets, regression thresholds, A/B test criteria, and automated rollback triggers that the Optimize product will use to accept or reject changes (model, quantization, batching, caching). The goal is to ensure durable output quality guarantees while enabling automated cost/perf improvements.
background: Optimize produces recommendations (batching, quantization, and model variant suggestions) and can automatically roll out weight changes or config changes on customer workloads. We need deterministic, measurable gating to avoid regressions in output quality. Current gaps: inconsistent prompt coverage, ambiguous thresholds, and no clear rollback policy for production rollouts.
goals: 1) Define a minimal canonical prompt set per workload category (chat, completion, rerank, embed-eval) that captures critical regressions. 2) Set statistically sound regression thresholds and power targets for A/B tests. 3) Specify deterministic rollback triggers and alerting for automated/managed rollouts. 4) Provide acceptance criteria and test plan that engineering can implement in the Optimize pipeline.
scope_in_scope:
- Create canonical prompt sets for three workload buckets (conversational, instruction completion, reranking)
- Define regression thresholds (absolute and relative) for quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, embedding cosine drop, task-specific accuracy, human eval proxies)
- A/B test statistical criteria (minimum sample size, significance levels)
- Automated rollback triggers (metric drops, error spikes, latency regressions)
- Integration points with Optimize CI and Console alerting
scope_out_of_scope:
- Building full human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows (we will provide hooks)
- End-to-end label collection for new customers
- Per-customer custom prompt sets beyond templated variants
requirements:
1) Prompt sets must be executable at scale: no dependency on private data, and each prompt must be deterministic given seed where applicable.
2) For each workload bucket define: 25 anchor prompts (10 core, 10 edge, 5 adversarial) as baseline.
3) Metrics to track: task accuracy/F1 (where labels exist), embedding cosine similarity delta, token-level perplexity change, contextual hallucination rate (auto-detected heuristics), and latency percentiles.
4) Regression thresholds: a) For task accuracy/F1: absolute drop > 2.5% or relative drop > 5% triggers fail; b) For embedding cosine: mean delta < -0.02 triggers fail; c) For hallucination heuristics: rate increase > 30% (relative) triggers fail; d) Latency: 95th percentile increase > 20% triggers fail.
5) A/B statistical rules: min effective sample size 1,000 served responses per variant (with at least 200 labeled items for labeled metrics), two-sided significance test at alpha=0.01 for critical metrics; use bootstrap CI for non-parametric metrics.
6) Rollout rules: canary at 1% for 24h, expand to 10% for 24h, expand to 50% for 48h, and full if no critical failures. Abort/rollback if any critical metric crosses threshold at any stage.
7) Console must surface a clear pass/fail decision and the delta with confidence intervals.
8) All thresholds and prompt sets must be configurable per-customer for Dedicated/Private later (initial defaults apply to hosted Optimize).
acceptance_criteria:
- A canonical prompt set exists for each workload bucket (files checked into evaluate/prompt-sets with metadata and tags).
- Automated evaluation pipeline runs against the prompt sets producing a standardized report with metric deltas and CI.
- The pipeline implements the regression thresholds above and returns explicit PASS/FAIL per metric and overall gating decision.
- A/B runner enforces the min sample size and significance rules and emits a summary suitable for Console and alerting.
- Rollout orchestrator consumes the evaluation output and will automatically pause/rollback if any fail condition is met.
- Product/PM, Eng, and Design have reviewed and signed off on thresholds for the initial hosted defaults.
- End-to-end smoke test demonstrating a simulated regression causing an automated rollback is documented and executed in staging.
success_metrics:
- 0 production incidents caused by Optimize auto-rollouts in the first 3 months post-release (target: 0).
- False-positive gating rate < 5% (i.e., accepted changes later judged as regressions by manual review).
- Time-to-detect regressions during a rollout < 30 minutes (median)
- Adoption: 30% of high-usage customers enable Optimize gated rollouts within 90 days
A_B_criteria:
- Primary metric depends on workload: accuracy/F1 for labeled tasks, mean embedding cosine for embeddings, normalized user-satisfaction proxy for chat.
- Hypothesis must specify primary metric and expected direction.
- Minimum sample size: 1,000 responses per arm with at least 200 labeled observations if metric requires labels.
- Statistical test: two-sided at alpha=0.01 for primary metric; secondary metrics reported with alpha=0.05 but do not gate rollout.
- Minimum detectable effect (MDE) guidance: For most customers set MDE at 2.5% relative for accuracy-like metrics or 0.02 absolute for embedding cosine.
- Use sequential testing safeguards: do not stop early unless crossing the pre-registered alpha boundary corrected for repeated looks (O'Brien-Fleming or alpha spending).
rollback_triggers:
- Automatic rollback triggers (any one causes immediate abort):
  1) Primary metric drop beyond configured threshold (see requirements).
  2) Runtime error rate spike > 1% absolute (from baseline).
  3) 95th percentile latency increase > 20% absolute.
  4) Severe downstream degradation detected by core product SLO monitors (external integration)
- Manual rollback triggers: a single SEV-high customer complaint tied to output correctness during rollout phase should trigger immediate human review and may result in rollback.
- Post-rollback: the system must capture the exact rollout snapshot, evaluation report, and a minimal set of logs for incident review.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement prompt sets and evaluation harness in repo evaluate/optimize.
2) Integrate evaluation harness into Optimize CI such that any change to model/config triggers a pre-rollout evaluation.
3) Canary rollout: 1% for 24h -> 10% for 24h -> 50% for 48h -> full.
4) Monitoring hooks: wire pass/fail outputs to Console, PagerDuty if critical.
5) Staging simulation: create a synthetic regression to validate automated rollback.
6) Document operational runbook and run a tabletop exercise with SRE and Support.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for metric computations and bootstrap CI modules.
- Integration tests that run canonical prompt sets against a reference and candidate model and verify the evaluation report format.
- Staging e2e test that simulates both safe and failing rollouts (forced metric failure) and validates automatic rollback behavior.
- A/B runner test harness to validate significance logic with synthetic traffic.
- UX validation: Console shows gating decision with delta and CI and a link to the failing artifacts.
notes:
- We intentionally choose conservative defaults for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private may tune thresholds.
- For hallucination heuristics we will iterate: initial heuristic is named-entity contradiction detector plus answer-length anomaly.
- Consider later expansion to continuous learning and label collection exports for customers.
- Coordinate with Legal for any dataset/public benchmark usage.
- Security review required for any prompt sets derived from customer data (flagged as to be configurable).
